scope.market: NSE cash equities, primarily point-in-time NIFTY 50 constituents

interpretation: The catalogue is a pre-registered research library of distinct practical hypotheses. It is not a claim that any strategy is profitable. Numerical permutations are deliberately bounded to reduce data-snooping risk.
universal_execution_invariants: Completed-bar decisions only; no same-bar look-ahead fills.
Daily context uses the previous completed session unless a true intraday daily feature is explicitly defined.
Exact effective-dated costs, slippage and impact are included in net P&L.
Finite-capital portfolio acceptance is separate from theoretical signal generation.
All runs persist source, code, strategy, feature, universe, calendar, fee and execution hashes.
Probability remains NOT_CALIBRATED until chronological out-of-sample calibration is accepted.
Partial/failed data sessions fail closed or are explicitly excluded and reported.

NG01.name: Data completeness and session integrity
NG01.rule: No signal when the symbol-session has missing mandatory bars, conflicting duplicates, invalid OHLC, unqualified corporate-action treatment, or a failed source checksum.

NG02.name: Point-in-time and warm-up integrity
NG02.rule: Every daily feature is through D-1; every intraday feature is from completed bars only; multi-timeframe features must be available before the decision and have declared warm-up.

NG03.name: Liquidity, cost and capacity hurdle
NG03.rule: Reject when estimated round-trip charges, slippage and impact consume the configured fraction of expected gross edge, or when volume/turnover cannot support the ticket size.

NG04.name: Volatility shock and VIX state
NG04.rule: Use a versioned VIX/ATR shock rule. Mean-reversion entries wait for stabilisation; breakout entries require broader confirmation rather than a single shock bar.

NG05.name: Market regime and breadth alignment
NG05.rule: Use NIFTY direction, breadth, participation, dispersion and above-VWAP ratios to distinguish trend, range, panic and narrow-leadership states.

NG06.name: Sector alignment
NG06.rule: Require the stock setup not to conflict materially with its sector trend unless the strategy is explicitly a sector-relative reversal.

NG07.name: Abnormal participation or operator-shock guard
NG07.rule: When volume, bar range and beta-adjusted residual movement are extreme but market/sector participation is narrow, do not immediately chase or fade; require a stabilisation or retest sequence.

NG08.name: Gap, event and corporate-action guard
NG08.rule: Classify opening gap magnitude and scheduled/corporate-action context. Treat unadjusted ex-date gaps or unexplained discontinuities as non-tradable data.

NG09.name: Time remaining and forced-exit risk
NG09.rule: Reject entries that do not leave enough time for the strategy’s historical target-time distribution; use family-specific latest-entry and maximum-hold rules.

NG10.name: Overextension and chase guard
NG10.rule: Avoid entries after excessive distance from VWAP/EMA/ATR or after multiple same-direction wide-range bars unless the strategy explicitly tests continuation after a retest.

NG11.name: Portfolio concentration and correlated exposure
NG11.rule: Apply total cash, maximum positions, sector limits, correlated-signal limits and deterministic signal ranking before a theoretical signal becomes an accepted trade.

NG12.name: Indicator redundancy and disagreement
NG12.rule: Do not count several oscillators derived from the same price path as independent evidence. Require at least one orthogonal confirmation such as volume, level, time or market state.

NG13.name: Intrabar ambiguity and fill feasibility
NG13.rule: Where stop and target coexist inside one bar, use tick data or conservative stop-first handling; record target touch separately from executable fill.

NG14.name: Historical/live feature parity
NG14.rule: The same feature version must produce equivalent values in batch replay and online calculation within declared tolerance.

EX01.name: Indicator reversal + ATR stop + time stop
EX01.rule: Exit on the strategy’s reversal condition, initial stop 0.75–1.25 ATR, maximum hold 90/120/135 minutes, and mandatory intraday close.

EX02.name: Executable net target + signal failure
EX02.rule: Exit at first executable price meeting the configured net target, or on setup failure, ATR stop, maximum hold, or mandatory close. Preserve target-touch and target-fill separately.

EX03.name: Breakout failure + ATR trail
EX03.rule: Exit on close back inside the broken range or below VWAP, plus initial ATR stop and optional chandelier/ATR trail; mandatory intraday close.

EX04.name: VWAP/EMA loss + time stop
EX04.rule: Exit when price loses the controlling VWAP/EMA on a completed bar, or at ATR stop, maximum hold, or mandatory close.

EX05.name: Swing ATR trail + time horizon
EX05.rule: Exit on 2–3 ATR trailing stop, trend failure, target multiple, or maximum 5/10/20-session holding horizon; calculate delivery costs and overnight gap risk.

EX06.name: Time-pattern close
EX06.rule: Enter only in the specified session window and exit at the defined later window or earlier risk failure. No overnight carry unless a separate swing version exists.

data_tiers.D1: Qualified stock OHLCV only; generally ten-year compatible after source qualification.
data_tiers.D2: Stock plus aligned NIFTY/sector/VIX OHLCV; ten-year compatible subject to timestamp and constituent mapping.
data_tiers.D3: Synchronized cross-sectional panel/breadth/volume-profile features; requires full panel assembly and point-in-time universe.

evidence_grades.A1: Directly aligned with a well-established empirical research family; transfer to Indian intraday equities still requires validation.
evidence_grades.A2: Uses research-supported components or market-microstructure findings in a practical hybrid.
evidence_grades.B1: Widely used practitioner rule with plausible mechanics and some/mixed empirical support.
evidence_grades.C1: Candlestick or geometric pattern with mixed evidence; never test or deploy as a standalone signal.
evidence_grades.CONTROL: Engine/economic control, not an alpha claim.

recommended_test_design.wave_1: 24 high-priority controls and strategies; synthetic/golden -> five-stock pilot -> one-year point-in-time universe.
recommended_test_design.wave_2: 36 additional mature strategies after Wave 1 engine, comparison and UI acceptance.
recommended_test_design.wave_3: 36 extended or more geometry/pattern-sensitive strategies after walk-forward governance is proven.
three_views_per_strategy: Common-exit signal study for comparable entry quality
